result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.maximal_matching()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a maximal matching in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21909-L21982){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.maximal_matching() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A maximal matching is a matching (set of edges with no shared endpoints) that cannot be extended by adding any other edge. Uses a greedy algorithm. Note that a maximal matching is not necessarily a maximum matching (largest possible). For weighted graphs, use `max_weight_matching()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs forming a maximal matching. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(E)` where `E` is the number of edges - space complexity: `O(V)` for tracking matched nodes - greedy algorithm: processes edges in arbitrary order - result may vary between calls due to iteration order - for maximum cardinality matching, use specialized algorithms - for weighted matching, use `max_weight_matching()` ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path of 6 nodes has exactly 3 disjoint edges available, so a maximal matching pairs every node: ::: {#264d40a2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(6) # 1-2-3-4-5-6 matching = graph.maximal_matching() # Returns 3 (e.g., edges 1-2, 3-4, 5-6) len(matching) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: The matched edges can be marked as an edge attribute for a quick visual check of which connections were paired up: ::: {#0cf1ca2c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_grid_2d(rows=4, cols=4) matching = graph.maximal_matching() # Color matched edges for visualization colors = {edge_id: "red" for edge_id in matching} graph.set_edge_attrs("color", colors) # Returns the number of matched edges len(matching) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 8 ``` ::: ::: In a complete graph with an even number of nodes, a maximal matching is also a perfect matching, pairing every single node: ::: {#6f5138d8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_full_graph(10) matching = graph.maximal_matching() # Returns 5 (all 10 nodes paired up) len(matching) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
